leads.summary: CLI toggles treat every unsuccessful IPC result as if no shell were running
leads.consequence: When a shell is running but has no bar yet (or an active replacement bar without these methods), the IPC method answers no-bar; omarchy-bar writes a shell.json fallback, prints 'Bar pills toggled' or 'Bar floating toggled', and exits successfully even though no running bar was toggled. An IPC timeout, unavailable method, or other shell error is also silently downgraded to an offline config edit; if the effective state came from a theme, that edit can select the wrong next state. The fallback is not limited to the promised no-shell case. Distinguish an offline connection failure from no-bar and other errors, and report non-offline failures instead of claiming success.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (stub-qs fallback matrix); Opus judged file-flip fallback reasonable and behaviour matches the old semantics; not a defect, not published

leads.summary: Another open PR changes the shared sampler's default output protocol
leads.location: bin/omarchy-bar-text-color:189-200; shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml:1184-1190; open PR #8615 bin/omarchy-bar-text-color patch
leads.consequence: If open PR #8615's default regions sampler is integrated without reconciling this PR's --inset/--blend arguments and single-color consumer, it prints three colors while this bar only accepts one, leaving transparent foreground sampling unapplied. This PR's bar-text-color-test.sh also expects single-color stdout, and its new sampler options are not recognized by #8615's option parser. Integrating both changes requires an explicit output and argument protocol choice, not simply applying the two patches together.
leads.triage: factual check: #8615 open (last updated 2026-09-08); the sampler flags come from carried commits c199c03c/06711828, not the new work; textual overlap a merge would surface; dropped from public comment, recorded in REPORT.md

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13140#issuecomment-5823989808) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13140#issuecomment-5829005744), checked at head `97118bab`.

**Verified:** all three earlier findings are resolved at this head. No regression was found in the code changed since `e084f68`. Two small documentation gaps and one optional test note remain.

| Earlier finding | Status at `97118bab` |
|---|---|
| Right-click held 200 ms or longer did not open the card | Resolved: `CenterGestureArea.onPressed` opens the card on a right press (`Bar.qml:1865`), and `onClicked` no longer does |
| Menu rows and `omarchy bar ... toggle` disagreed with the card | Resolved: `toggle_in_shell` calls the new `toggleBarPills` / `toggleBarFloating` IPC methods, which run the card's own `togglePills()` / `toggleFloating()` |
| `manual/05-the-top-bar.md` did not cover the new switches | Resolved: the manual now describes the right-click switches, says "left click-and-hold", lists all four Style > Menu Bar items and adds both commands |

**Verified details:**

- **Opening on press:** press-and-hold still starts a move only with the left button, and double-click and release handling are unchanged. The card's `HyprlandFocusGrab` includes the bar window, and in Hyprland v0.56.2 a button press outside the grabbed surfaces clears the grab, but a release does not. So releasing the right button on the bar does not close a card opened on that press (traced from source, not observed in a running session).
- **IPC toggle:** with a running bar, the three cases from the earlier table now match the card. Widget pills come back as `widget` after off/on within a session, and theme-default floating or pills turn off on the first press. Any answer other than `ok` falls back to the old `shell.json` flip and exits 0: no bar, a shell without the new method, not ready, not running, or a timeout. The description's "since the shell started" wording matches the code.
- **Other changes since `e084f68`:** the `BarModel.js` helpers `windowMargins` and `exclusiveZone` compute the same values as the inline code they replace, and `anchorOffset` places the anchored centre widget where `anchors.centerIn` puts it without pills. `KeyboardPanel.qml` and notification placement reduce to the old values for a flush bar. The tray foreground is unchanged with pills off.

**Documentation:**

- The IPC method table in `docs/omarchy-shell.md:113-132` lists `toggleBarTransparency` but not `toggleBarPills` or `toggleBarFloating`, which `omarchy bar pills|floating toggle` now depend on.
- `shell/plugins/bar/README.md:19` still says "(or click-and-hold)" where the manual now says "left click-and-hold".

**Optional test improvement:** the press-and-hold guard check in `test/shell.d/bar-test.sh:27` still passes when `|| !(gestureArea.pressedButtons & Qt.LeftButton)` is removed from `Bar.qml` (checked with a modified copy), so the left-button-only rule is not under test. Adding a separate `pressedButtons\s*&\s*Qt\.LeftButton` term to that pattern would cover it.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up review of head `97118bab6ff1315a655ff10442d166b68689e005` against the earlier head `e084f68` and merge base `28ceaae`: source review plus sandboxed test runs. `bar-test.sh` (175 checks) and `menu-test.sh` (123 checks) passed. `config-test.sh` needs a separate `omarchy-pkgs` checkout for an unrelated PKGBUILD block. With that block removed from a copy, it passed all 34 checks, including the 5 new cases. The IPC fallback was exercised with the real `omarchy-bar` and `omarchy-shell` against a stub `qs`, not a live shell. Upstream source read: Qt Declarative 6.11.2, Quickshell v0.3.1, Hyprland v0.56.2; installed versions were not checked. No GUI, Quickshell or Hyprland session was run, so input timing, popup placement and focus-grab behaviour were not observed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
